title: A 700-Year-Old Skeleton May Preserve Evidence of an Ancient Punishment
mediaSource: medieval China skeleton nasal amputation CT Sanzhiyuan cemetery archaeology

scenes.title: A strange cut appeared in a 700-year-old woman's facial bones
scenes.narration: CT scans of a medieval skeleton from Henan, China, revealed damage suggesting that parts of the nose had been deliberately removed.
keywords: medieval China skeleton nasal amputation CT

scenes.title: The damage did not look like a normal accident
scenes.narration: Parts of the nasal bones were missing, yet nearby facial bones and front teeth showed no major trauma expected from a severe fall or impact.

scenes.title: Ancient texts describe nose cutting as punishment
scenes.narration: Chinese historical records repeatedly mention nasal amputation as a punishment designed to leave a permanent visible mark.

scenes.title: But skeletal evidence has been extremely rare
scenes.narration: Written accounts survive, but archaeologists have had very little physical evidence showing that this punishment was actually carried out.

scenes.title: Researchers say punishment is the most likely explanation
scenes.narration: Based on the location and pattern of the cuts, the team argues that deliberate punitive nasal amputation is the strongest interpretation.

scenes.title: A punishment known from texts may have left a mark on bone
scenes.narration: A practice described for centuries in written records may now have a direct physical trace in the remains of one medieval woman.
